Prepare each topic below in the background, so its card carries your proposal by the time the user opens it. Nobody reads your replies: only what you store counts. Run every command as `cd {SRC}/agent-skills-demo && python# {HOME}/.claude/skills/rework-mr/scripts/threads.py <command> --iid #`. Store with `propose` (or `keep-plan`, below) and nothing else: never edit code, commit, push, post, resolve, or show anything (no `set`, `agree`, `post`, `open`, `later`, `quote --focus`, `show_topic`). Read first: `bodies` (every open thread, first and last comment), then `quote <t>` for each topic (the code the comment is on and the whole thread), then the code itself where the point needs it. For each, store one proposal: `propose <t> --says needs|fyi --why "<#–# English sentences: what the reviewer asks, what the code does, and the trade-off; end on a **Recommendation:** sentence>" [--summary "<English one-liner>"] [--outcome fix|reply|push-back|question --plan "<one sentence: what to do>"] [--answer-now] [--change - <<'CHANGE_EOF' … CHANGE_EOF]`. `fyi` where the comment asks nothing of the user (a thank-you, an OK on what they did): no outcome then. `needs` takes `--outcome` and `--plan`; `fix` for every plan that changes code, a push-back that also adds a comment included, the others for a plan that only replies. For a small fix add `--change -` with the change on stdin as `@@ <path>:<first>-<last>` blocks, each followed by the new lines that replace those lines (the diff is built from the file; never write one by hand): the idea and its main change at its origin (the rename where the name is defined, the new parameter in the signature), never the call sites it adapts. `--answer-now` on a fix whose plan answers the reviewer ahead of it: they asked a question, or offered options and the plan picks one. In `--why` and `--plan` alike, every identifier, path and value in backticks: the card draws them as code. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. End with one line saying what you stored.
